This is the classic Exercism "connect" (Hex) problem. The board is a rhombus, and each row is indented by one space. Player X connects left and right, and player O connects top and bottom.

Standard approach: parse the board into a grid. Each row r (0-indexed) has r leading spaces, and the length of row r is n (for an n×n board). A cell at row r, column c (c is 0..n-1) is adjacent to:
- (r, c-1), (r, c+1) — same row
- (r-1, c-1), (r-1, c) — row above
- (r+1, c), (r+1, c+1) — row below

X wins if it connects the left edge to the right edge: a cell is on the left edge when c == 0, and on the right edge when c == n-1... actually, for a rhombus, the left edge is column 0 of each row, and the right edge is the last column of each row. O wins if it connects the top (row 0) to the bottom (the last row).

    """Compute the winner of a game of Hex / Polygon (Connect).

    The board is a parallelogram of hexagonal fields drawn as rows of
    two-character cells, each row indented one space further than the
    previous one.  Player ``X`` connects the left side to the right

    # west, east, upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right.
    # Because each row is shifted one cell half-width to the right, the
    # diagonals are (row +/- 1, col +/- 1) with *opposite* signs; a
    # straight (row +/- 1, col +/- 1) staircase is not a legal move.
    _NEIGHBOURS = ((0, -1), (0, 1), (-1, 0), (-1, 1), (1, -1), (1, 0))

        self.rows = [line.split() for line in board.strip().splitlines()]

    def get_winner(self):
        if self._connects("X"):
            return "X"
        if self._connects("O"):
            return "O"
        return ""

        rows = self.rows
        if not rows:
